correctness.rationale: The derivation condition is equivalent by direct Leibniz expansion to \(A^T+A=cI_m\) and an arbitrary central row, with converse. In characteristic two the central scalar vanishes and every symmetric A appears. Counting symmetric ranks by unique radicals and the verified nonsingular-block recurrence gives \(N_r\) and hence the displayed complete \(C_j\) via row-span choices. For \(m=3\) and odd q the determinant \(t(t^2+a^2+b^2+c^2)\), ternary quadratic-level count \(q^2+q\), and a rank-two lower bound in singular t≠0 case prove the entire vector. Independent enumeration of all 512/2187/78125 parametrized derivations over F2/F3/F5, explicit derivation linear-constraint dimension checks, and exhaustive symmetric rank checks over F4 dimension3 and F2 dimension4 all passed. Limits: finite experiments do not prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: Derivation ranks are intrinsic algebra invariants, with invertible derivations a natural structural existence question. The entire even-characteristic spectrum in every dimension m≥2 is a motivated exact finite-field invariant. It quantifies the global disappearance of invertible derivations and an unbounded m−1 exceptional-characteristic dimension jump, plus all ranks for the canonical four-dimensional algebra over both parity classes. The precise distribution is not simply a selected experimental point or arbitrary cutoff; it resolves every rank stratum of a stable algebraic family and supports future arithmetic comparisons of derivation varieties.
